description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add: lib/zaq/contracts/record/authorization.ex and provenance.ex; test/zaq/contracts/record_test.exs and record/authorization_test.exs. Share Authorization's effective-principal precedence with Provenance's signature projection without changing can?/filter semantics. Bind nested principal overrides, malformed/unmatched nested principals and flat provider fields so an attacker cannot change the authorization principal while retaining a valid signature. Preserve provider projection and semantically equivalent flat signatures where unchanged. Earlier nested-principal signatures that omitted the effective principal fail closed and require authorized metadata re-fetch/reissue; no insecure legacy verification fallback or blanket database rewrite.
Tests to add before implementation: preserve current Record and Authorization suites. Add nested/flat, atom/string, equivalent normalization and conflicting override cases; tamper type/key/rights after sealing and assert verify/from_map/schema rejection; malformed nested principal must not alias a valid flat grant. Add property tests that authorization-changing mutations invalidate signatures and valid JSON-safe records round-trip. Test nil actor denies, explicit literal bypass does not skip authenticity, and re-fetch/reseal restores valid authorized use without token fallback.
Branches/paths validated: nested principal wins over flat fields; flat fallback only when permitted by existing Authorization; missing/invalid principal, case/space normalization, unloaded versus empty permissions, wrong signature and old unsafe projection. Preserve existing permission behavior and valid source producers.
Mocking plan: none for pure signatures/authorization; use real Person/permission fixtures and isolated runtime dependencies already supported by Provenance. Do not stub internal permission checks.
Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content: Authorization/Provenance public contract and docs/services/agent.md or materialization.md for the precise token compatibility/reissue rule; no claim that provenance itself grants access.
Action reuse assessment: extend existing Record.Authorization/Provenance, not a new permission Action. These are shared contracts with no delivery side effects. Input Record/permission maps -> canonical effective principal and authentic claims or existing errors; caller authorization remains separate. Preserve current callers, expose only the smallest shared projection needed, and verify with producer/consumer regressions before Action integration.

Implementation handoff: Scope and sequence approved by the user on 2026-11-28. This turn records the plan only; application implementation, commits, pushes, rebases and dependency publication are not performed or authorized by this planning update. Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/documentation.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md before execution. Read applicable service guides and module responsibilities; Agent work requires the harness-critical checks; BO work requires DESIGN.md and docs/bo-components.md. Recheck live source and dependency contracts. Preserve existing test behavior unless specifically approved. Write immediate unit/integration/property tests before corresponding code; new browser journeys wait for the human UX gate. Keep real internal boundaries, mock only external edges, and inject runtime dependencies through existing opts/context and Zaq.Config. Follow the owning validation lifecycle. PR7 owns RunAgent, NotifyPerson and notification/workflow integration.

comments.text: Pre-implementation discovery only while .1 setup runs. Module-context evidence: Authorization.can?/3 -> permission_matches? -> principal currently prioritizes a nested principal map and otherwise principal_channel/principal_type + principal_key; comparisons normalize identifiers. Provenance.issue/seal -> canonical_claims -> permission_projection currently signs a different provider-flat principal projection, omitting nested authorization identity. Record.from_map and semantic Zoi validate via Provenance.verify; metadata producers reseal. No process/global selection state is involved. Extend the existing Authorization principal projection for shared use, retain can?/filter semantics and provider signature fields, bind effective-principal overrides and malformed nested cases; no new permission Action/ACL implementation. Source reference branch has a related example but is not authority. Risks to cover: flat signature compatibility, nested overrides/tampering, invalid nested versus flat fallback, rights, atom/string maps, old unsafe nested signatures and JSON round trips. Existing Record/Authorization tests remain unchanged; add focused tests/properties. Serena overviews/targeted symbol reads worked; references query could not resolve the reported permission_projection name, so bounded rg established local callers. No production edits before .1 readiness.

Added a new isolated ProvenanceTest file before production changes; existing tests untouched. Covers nested identity escalation as a property, canonical principal precedence, type/key/rights mutation across verify/from_map/Zoi, malformed nested identity versus valid flat fallback, independent provider/channel bindings, flat projection compatibility, unsafe old-token reissue, nil actor denial, equivalent normalization and signed JSON round trips. Current .1 baseline test process is still compiling dependencies; production remains unchanged until the new tests are observed red. Compatibility choice: nested maps always require explicit effective-principal binding, including when equivalent to flat fields, so old unsafe nested signatures cannot silently retain validity.

Observed red phase: new suite 4/11 passed, with 7 failures proving nested identity escalation, unmatched and malformed nested/flat projection aliasing, channel override and unsafe legacy signature acceptance; shared principal API absent as expected. Implemented the smallest shared extension: expose Authorization.principal/1 without changing its body/can?/filter; Provenance retains provider fields and includes the effective principal when nested or different from the provider projection. Nested maps always bind even when equivalent to flat, enforcing explicit legacy reissue. Owning Agent documentation describes compatibility/authenticity versus authorization. No PR4/PR5 defect discovered or code changed there.

Continuation verification: preserved existing uncommitted provenance implementation and tests. Fresh isolated Record, Authorization and Provenance run passed: 57 checks (3 properties, 54 examples). mix q passed. No existing assertions changed. Effective-principal binding preserves flat signatures while requiring nested legacy metadata reissue.

title: [zaq-pi3.2] Bind signed provenance to effective authorization principals
